subject.title: [Bug]:  [Windows] exec spawn: all commands hang with no output (stdio pipe deadlock)

question: Should this issue wait for native Windows reproduction before any fix attempt, or should maintainers queue an exploratory Windows debug pass now?
rationale: Current source is relevant but inconclusive, and a speculative code change could target the wrong process path without native Windows evidence.

options.title: Require Native Repro First
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer or reporter captures a native Windows gateway run showing stdout/stderr, PID, exit state, timeout behavior, and process tree for `echo hello` and `node -v`.

options.title: Queue Exploratory Debug Pass
options.body: Have a Windows-capable maintainer investigate both supervisor and direct helper paths, but do not start an automated fix PR until the failing boundary is identified.

recommendation.title: Require Native Repro First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer or reporter captures a native Windows gateway run showing stdout/stderr, PID, exit state, timeout behavior, and process tree for `echo hello` and `node -v`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent current-main touches and prior Windows exec invocation history in the implicated process paths.
